analysis_status: exploratory follow-up; epoch-selection rule frozen before Q8-E001 target evaluation, but developed after prior Q5-Q8 exploration on BNCI2014_001
research_question: Does source-only mean-rank aggregation of the frozen Q5 inner validation trajectories provide a more robust training-duration selection procedure than Q5 mean validation CE?
hypothesis: Mean within-fold epoch ranks reduce sensitivity to validation-subject CE scale heterogeneity; target-performance improvement is not assumed.

training.epoch_selection: earliest epoch minimizing equal-inner-fold mean within-fold validation-CE rank, using frozen Q5 inner learning curves

evaluation.target_information: No target-subject fit, normalization, early stopping, seed choice, or hyperparameter tuning
evaluation.primary_population: all trials including expert artifact flags
evaluation.primary_metric: subject-level balanced_accuracy, then equal-subject mean of three-seed means
evaluation.parent_comparator: Q5-E001 frozen raw-EEG mean-validation-CE EEGNet baseline
evaluation.inference: exploratory paired subject contrasts; nine held-out subjects are the inference units; seed fits are not independent subjects

resource_benchmark.note: Synthetic shape-matched CPU benchmark only, not EEG classification or model selection.

limitations: BNCI data and Q4 comparator were previously explored; this is not an independent confirmatory study.
Forty-epoch cap is compute-bounded; a selected boundary epoch indicates possible undertraining.
Offline zero-phase run filtering is not a causal online pipeline.
Braindecode EEGNet here is not the original paper's exact preprocessing or split reproduction.
The mean-rank rule was motivated by post-Q5/Q6/Q7/Q8-A001-A003 analyses on the same dataset; Q8-E001 is therefore not independent external confirmation.
Q8-E001 reuses frozen Q5 source-validation curves and trains only new final models at the pre-frozen mean-rank epochs.
